task.description: ACS task id (HACK-NN) or GitHub issue

rules: ABA is the app builder (Pukujan/app-builder-automation, dyad headless) and runs on the MacBook Pro; it builds only application code: backend app/ and server.py, frontend web/, and the Octo schema/ and migrations/
ABA never files or edits issues; it receives an already-filed issue number and builds against that issue
ABA never writes docs/, contracts/ or .github/; specs, docs, PR prose, contracts, CI and issue logs belong to the other agents
ABA chooses its own implementation and its own frontend dependencies inside web/; no issue, spec, handoff or contract prescribes its technology

ABA does not change Python dependencies or requirements files; if a Python dependency seems necessary, stop and report it to the coordinating agent, which owns requirements.in, the uv lock and tools/dep_policy.py
Never write vendored ACS files (acs/seat_protocol.py, acs/watchdog_check.py, acs/LICENSE.acs, acs/assignment.schema.json)
Never commit cache/, runs/, data/, logs/ or any secret
Check repo.manifest.json before adding a top-level file or folder

Never hand-write custom code when mature OSS or an existing tool plus thin glue code can do the job; manual coding is allowed only for confirmed debugging or fixing logic pipelines (AGENTS.md, Reuse before you write)

A PR that adds a source file or more than 150 non-test lines under app/, acs/ or tools/ needs an 'OSS considered' section naming a specific project or SDK and why it does not fit, or a bugfix label or line plus Closes #N for an issue with confirmed evidence; tools/pr_policy.py enforces it in gates
Call providers through their official SDK when one exists instead of raw httpx or requests (AGENTS.md, Dependencies and SDKs)
